document_summary: Berkeley Rent Board web page on tenant screening and application fees, covering California Civil Code 1950.6 and Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.78 (Berkeley, CA).

rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap (Civ. Code § 1950.6)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge applicants a screening fee only up to an annually adjusted maximum, and must give a receipt, an itemized list of expenses and a refund of any unused portion. No fee may be charged if no unit is available, and the landlord must accept a reusable screening report if the applicant provides one.
rules.key_value: $68.96 maximum screening fee for 2026 (figure as published by the Berkeley Rent Board)
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to prospective tenants of residential rental units in California.
rules.interaction: Berkeley BMC 13.78.010 adds a local disclosure duty on top of the state cap; it does not change the cap.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96
rules.conflict_note: Open question: § 1950.6 has no single official 2026 dollar figure. This Berkeley page gives $68.96, but the statute itself and other sources are not in this capture, so the figure may differ elsewhere.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source for state law; the page does not state when the 2026 figure took effect, so effective_date is null. Return deadline for the credit report (7 days) and the refund and first-qualified-applicant policy options are folded into the requirement.

rules.title: Notification of state law limitation on tenant screening fees (BMC 13.78.010)
rules.requirement: An owner who charges a fee for a credit report and application processing must give the applicant, in the application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
rules.key_value: Required disclosure of the Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the state maximum fee cap before collecting the fee
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners or agents receiving a request to rent residential property in Berkeley who charge a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review or otherwise process an application.
rules.interaction: Local disclosure duty that layers on top of the state cap in Civ. Code § 1950.6; it sets no separate local dollar cap.
rules.quoted_span: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b).
rules.extraction_notes: The page does not state an adoption or effective date, so both are null. The page notes the URL in the statement is still to be provided by the City. Under BMC 13.78.018, chapter 13.78 applies regardless of contrary lease language.

rules.title: Prohibition of non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies (BMC 13.78.016)
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or to adding or replacing a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.key_value: Ban on non-refundable renewal and roommate-change fees charged to existing tenants
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley (or their agents) and existing tenants.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.extraction_notes: The page does not state an adoption or effective date, so both are null.
